dc41.title: Retro board: undo / redo
dc41.summary: A sticky-note retro board already adds, edits and deletes notes. Add an undo/redo history with buttons and Ctrl/Cmd+Z.
dc41.brief:
Pinboard is a team retro board. App.tsx has Header, Toolbar, NoteCard and App. You can already add a note (in the picked color), type in it, and delete it. getBoard() in api.ts loads the notes after a random 0.3–0.9 s.

Product wants undo and redo. Read components/IconButton.tsx (use it for the new buttons) and utils/id.ts first.

The interesting decision is the shape of the state: right now it is one notes array. Undo needs the old versions too.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Change: cap history at 20 (~26 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan · 7–26 Core · 26–30 change · 30–36 Next · 36–38 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Every change to the notes becomes a snapshot. I'll replace notes with one state object { past, present, future } so the three always change together. Add and delete call commit(next): push present onto past, set the new present, clear future. Undo pops past into present and pushes the old present onto future; redo is the mirror. I'll write those as pure functions (h) => newH so I can pass them straight to setHistory, and the keydown effect doesn't need any dependencies.

Typing is the tricky part: one undo per keystroke would be awful. I'll update present without a history entry while typing, remember a snapshot on focus in a useRef, and on blur commit that snapshot to past if the notes changed. Can-undo / can-redo are derived from the array lengths."
requirements: Toolbar gets Undo and Redo buttons (use IconButton). Undo is disabled when there is nothing to undo, Redo when there is nothing to redo. Loading the board is not an undoable step

Adding and deleting a note can be undone and redone. A deleted note comes back in the same position. Doing a new action after an undo clears the redo stack. Typing still edits the text (it just doesn't create history entries yet)
Editing a note's text is one undo step per edit (commit when the note loses focus), not one step per keystroke

Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes and Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+Z redoes. While the cursor is in a note's textarea the shortcut is left to the browser (native text undo). The keydown listener is added once in an effect and removed in the cleanup; no stale state (undo twice quickly must undo two steps)

change.title: Cap the history at 20
change.html:
"On long retros the history grows forever and we keep every snapshot in memory."

  • Keep at most 20 undo steps. The oldest step is dropped when a 21st is added.
  • Show a small meter next to the buttons: "3 / 20" (undo steps available / max).

Hint: one .slice(-20) in the right place. Check that every path that pushes to past uses it.

hints: State shape: type History = { past: Note[][]; present: Note[]; future: Note[][] }. The notes you render are history.present.
Write pure helpers outside the component: function undoHistory(h: History): History { ... }. Then setHistory(undoHistory) works from a button and from a keydown listener with [] deps.
Commit: return { past: [...h.past, h.present], present: next, future: [] };. Undo: take the last item of past, put the old present at the front of future.
Keyboard: if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key.toLowerCase() === "z"). With Shift held, e.key is uppercase "Z", hence toLowerCase(). Search: "mdn KeyboardEvent metaKey".
Skip the shortcut while typing: const t = e.target as HTMLElement; if (t.tagName === "TEXTAREA") return;
Text edits: onFocus stores editStart.current = history.present; typing does setHistory((h) => ({ ...h, present: next })); onBlur pushes editStart.current onto past if h.present !== editStart.current.
rubric: Chose a single history object (past / present / future) and explained why
Undo / redo / commit are pure and never mutate arrays
Buttons' disabled states are derived from stack lengths, not stored
Keydown listener cleaned up; updater form avoids stale closures
Typing does not create one history entry per keystroke
Cap applied to every path that grows the past stack
Talked through edge cases (redo cleared after a new action, load not undoable)

primitives.name: slice() with negative numbers
primitives.note: Returns a new array (never mutates). Negative numbers count from the end. .slice(-20) is the whole "cap at 20" change.

primitives.name: Last item: at(-1)
primitives.note: Returns the item, or undefined for an empty array, so check the length first.

primitives.name: Add to the front with spread
primitives.example:
const future = ['b', 'c'];
['a', ...future]          // ['a', 'b', 'c']
primitives.note: Builds a new array; the original is untouched. Use it for the redo stack (newest first).

primitives.name: Pass a function to setState
primitives.example:
function undoHistory(h: History): History { ... }
setHistory(undoHistory); // React calls it with the latest state
primitives.note: React calls your function with the current state and stores what it returns, so a pure helper works from a button or a keydown listener without stale state.

dc42.title: Photo feed: infinite scroll
dc42.summary: A dark photo feed only shows the first page. Load the next page automatically when the user nears the bottom, using IntersectionObserver.
dc42.brief:
Aperture is a photo community. App.tsx has TopBar, Feed and App; cards are rendered by components/PhotoCard.tsx, and components/Spinner.tsx is a loading row you should reuse. The feed scrolls inside its own container (.feed-scroll), not the window.

getPhotos(cursor) returns { photos, nextCursor } after 0.5–1.1 s. nextCursor is null on the last page (40 photos in total). It logs every request to the console, so you can see duplicate loads.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4. Change: "Back to top" button (~20 min).

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan · 5–20 Core · 20–26 change · 26–28 Next · 28–30 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"State in Feed: photos, nextCursor (start at 0, null means done) and loading. I'll put an empty sentinel div after the last card and observe it with an IntersectionObserver whose root is the scroll container, not the viewport. When it intersects and nothing is in flight, I fetch the next page and append.

The observer callback is a closure, so for the in-flight guard I'll use a useRef; a state value would be stale inside it. The effect depends on nextCursor: each page recreates the observer, and if the sentinel is still visible it fires again, which fills tall screens. When nextCursor is null the effect just doesn't observe, and I show "You're all caught up". Cleanup disconnects."
requirements: The first page loads on mount (no button). When the user scrolls near the bottom of .feed-scroll, the next page is fetched with the previous nextCursor and appended. Use an IntersectionObserver on a sentinel element with the scroll container as root (not a scroll event)
While a page is loading, a loading row ("Loading more photos…", reuse Spinner) shows at the bottom of the list
No duplicate requests: scrolling up and down while a request is in flight never starts a second one, and no photo appears twice
At the end (nextCursor === null) the observer stops and the list ends with "You're all caught up · 40 photos". The observer is disconnected on unmount

change.title: Back to top
change.html:
"After 40 photos, getting back to the top is painful."

  • Once the feed is scrolled more than 800px, show a floating pill "↑ Back to top" centered at the bottom of the feed.
  • Clicking it smooth-scrolls the feed container to the top; the button disappears when back near the top.

Search: "mdn element scrollTo behavior smooth". The button needs a position: relative parent that does not scroll.

hints: You need two refs: scrollRef on .feed-scroll (the observer root) and sentinelRef on an empty div after the cards.
Search: "mdn IntersectionObserver root rootMargin". new IntersectionObserver(cb, { root: scrollRef.current, rootMargin: "0px 0px 300px 0px" }) starts loading 300px before the end.
Why a ref for the in-flight flag? The callback was created when the effect ran; a loading state value inside it is frozen at that moment. inFlight.current is always current.
Effect shape: useEffect(() => { if (nextCursor === null) return; const obs = new IntersectionObserver(...); obs.observe(sentinelRef.current); return () => { obs.disconnect(); }; }, [nextCursor]);

Inside the callback: if (!entries[0].isIntersecting || inFlight.current) return; inFlight.current = true; getPhotos(cursor).then((page) => { setPhotos((prev) => [...prev, ...page.photos]); setNextCursor(page.nextCursor); inFlight.current = false; });
rubric: Observer root is the feed's scroll container, not the window
In-flight guard explained (ref vs stale state in a closure)
Appends with the updater form; never duplicates
Stops cleanly at the end and disconnects on cleanup
Loading and end states are separate decisions above the return
Back-to-top derived from scrollTop with a threshold; smooth scroll on the container
Mentioned the alternative (scroll listener + math) and why the observer is better

notes: absolute · bottom 20 · centered · h 36 · pill · 13/700 · shadow 0 6 20

primitives.name: IntersectionObserver
primitives.syntax:
const io = new IntersectionObserver(callback, { root, rootMargin });
io.observe(el);   io.disconnect();
primitives.note: Calls you back when el enters / leaves root (default: the viewport, so pass the scroll container). rootMargin fires early. Always disconnect() in the effect cleanup.

primitives.name: useRef as a mutable flag
primitives.note: Changing .current does not re-render, and callbacks always read the latest value (state inside an old closure would be stale).

primitives.name: Append a page
primitives.note: Spread both arrays into a new one. Use the updater form so two quick loads never overwrite each other.

primitives.name: Smooth scroll a container
primitives.example:
scrollRef.current.scrollTop        // 1240 (px scrolled)
scrollRef.current.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' });
primitives.note: scrollTop reads how far an element is scrolled; scrollTo moves it. Read it in onScroll with e.currentTarget.scrollTop.

dc43.title: Playlist: drag to reorder
dc43.summary: Reorder a playlist with HTML5 drag and drop (plus accessible Move up/down buttons) and flag unsaved changes.
dc43.brief:
Sunday Slow Mornings is a playlist page. App.tsx has PlaylistHeader, TrackRow, TrackList and App. App already keeps its own tracks copy in state and has a working Save order button (savePlaylistOrder(trackIds), 0.6–1.2 s, shows "Saving…"). getPlaylist() takes 0.4–1.0 s.

Read utils/array.ts first: moveItem(list, from, to) is a pure helper that returns a reordered copy. utils/time.ts has formatDuration / formatTotal; components/Cover.tsx draws album art. Nothing can be reordered yet: that is your job.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Change: "Unsaved changes" indicator (~27 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan · 7–27 Core · 27–32 change · 32–38 Next · 38–40 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"tracks is already state, and moveItem exists, so every reorder is setTracks((prev) => moveItem(prev, from, to)) through one handleMove. For drag: dragId in state on dragstart (fades the row), and the hovered row as dropTarget. On dragover I preventDefault, or drop never fires. On drop I turn ids into indexes and call handleMove; dragend clears both, so a drop outside the list still resets.

Next: the before / after half from the mouse Y against the row's midpoint (and the index shift: removing the dragged row moves later rows up by one), then ▲ / ▼ buttons as the accessible path, through the same handleMove, with a polite live region."
requirements: Each row is draggable (with a ⋮⋮ handle). While dragging, the dragged row is faded (.is-dragging); the fade is cleared on drop and on dragend (dropped outside the list)

Dropping a row on another row moves the track to that row's position (reuse moveItem from utils/array.ts; never mutate). Track numbers always show the current position, and the existing Save order button saves the new order
A drop indicator line shows above or below the hovered row, depending on which half the pointer is over; dropping on the lower half places the track after that row
Each row has ▲ / ▼ buttons with aria-label="Move {title} up" / "… down", disabled on the first / last row. A visually hidden aria-live region announces "{title} moved to position 3 of 8"

Running time: the header shows the total ("Arvind · 8 songs · 30 min", formatTotal) and each row shows "starts 4:11", both recalculated on every reorder. A Discard button restores the last saved order

change.title: Unsaved changes
change.html:
"People reorder the playlist and leave without saving."

  • Show "● Unsaved changes" while the order differs from the last saved order, and "✓ All changes saved" otherwise.
  • Save order is disabled when nothing changed. Moving a track and moving it back must be clean again.

Hint: keep savedIds (what the server has), set on load and after a successful save. "Dirty" is derived by comparing id lists.

hints: Search: "mdn html drag and drop api". You need draggable, onDragStart, onDragOver (call e.preventDefault()!), onDrop and onDragEnd.
In onDragStart call e.dataTransfer.setData("text/plain", id); Firefox will not start a drag without data.
The rows need drag props, so render TrackRows straight from App (or pass the handlers through TrackList). The move itself: setTracks((prev) => { return moveItem(prev, from, to); });
Drop index: const from = tracks.findIndex((t) => t.id === dragId); let to = tracks.findIndex((t) => t.id === targetId); then handleMove(from, to).

Before / after (Next): const rect = e.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect(); const after = e.clientY > rect.top + rect.height / 2;. If after, to += 1; then if (from < to) to -= 1 (removing the dragged row shifts everything after it).
Dirty (change): tracks.map((t) => t.id).join(",") !== savedIds.join(","), derived, never stored. Start times (Stretch): a running total in a forEach above the return, then starts[i] in the map.
rubric: One move path (moveItem from utils) shared by drag and the buttons
dragover preventDefault and the index-shift edge case handled
Indicator state cleared on drop and on dragend (also when dropped outside)
Buttons are a real keyboard / screen reader alternative (labels, disabled ends, live region)
Save shows pending state; savedIds updated only after success
Totals, start times and dirty flag derived, not stored
Explained why not to keep index-based keys

notes: inset box-shadow 3px coral, top or bottom

primitives.name: HTML drag and drop events
primitives.syntax: <li draggable={true} onDragStart={...} onDragOver={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); }} onDrop={...} onDragEnd={...}>
primitives.example: onDragOver={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); }}  // without this, onDrop never fires
primitives.note: The browser only allows a drop where dragover was cancelled. dragend fires on the dragged element even when the drop lands outside, so clean up there.
primitives.search: mdn html drag and drop api

primitives.name: dataTransfer.setData()
primitives.note: Returns nothing. Firefox does not start a drag without some data; React state (dragId) is still the simplest place to keep what is being dragged.

primitives.name: findIndex()
primitives.note: Returns the index of the first match, or -1. Use it to turn the dragged / target ids into positions.

primitives.name: splice() on a copy (how moveItem works)
primitives.syntax: const next = [...list]; const [item] = next.splice(from, 1); next.splice(to, 0, item);
primitives.note: splice mutates and returns the removed items, which is why moveItem copies first. Never splice an array from state.

primitives.name: Compare two orders with join()
primitives.example:
['t1', 't2'].join(',') === ['t1', 't2'].join(',')   // true
['t1', 't2'] === ['t1', 't2']                       // false (different arrays)
primitives.note: === on arrays compares identity, not contents. Joining the ids into a string is a quick contents check for the "unsaved" flag.

dc44.title: Command palette (⌘K)
dc44.summary: A deploy dashboard already has every action as data. Build the Ctrl/Cmd+K palette: open / close, fuzzy filter, click to run; then arrow keys, ARIA and focus restore.
dc44.brief:
Orbit is a deploy dashboard. App.tsx has Sidebar, TopBar (with a "Search or run a command… ⌘K" button that does nothing yet), DeploymentList and App. Read commands.ts first: buildCommands(actions) already returns every action as { id, label, section, run }, and App already builds the list.

The codebase also has components/Modal.tsx (backdrop + centered dialog, calls onClose on a backdrop click), utils/fuzzy.ts (fuzzyMatch(text, query)) and components/Kbd.tsx (key caps). Your job is the palette itself. Each command's run() changes something visible (page, theme, sidebar, a queued deployment, a toast).

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Change: section headers (~28 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan · 7–28 Core · 28–33 change · 33–38 Next · 38–40 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"App owns paletteOpen, because both the shortcut and the top-bar button open it. The palette is its own component inside Modal, only rendered while open, so its query resets on every open and autoFocus works each time. Results are derived with fuzzyMatch. The ⌘K listener lives in an effect with cleanup and preventDefaults the browser shortcut; Escape is handled on the input.

Next: an active index (reset to 0 when the query changes) that the arrows move with wrapping, Enter runs results[active], aria-activedescendant so screen readers follow, and a returnFocus ref so an effect can put focus back when it closes."
requirements: Ctrl/Cmd+K anywhere (and clicking the top-bar search button) opens the palette in a Modal (centered over a dimmed backdrop) with the input focused. Pressing it again, Escape, or clicking the backdrop closes it. The browser's own Ctrl+K is prevented
Typing filters the commands with fuzzyMatch from utils/fuzzy.ts ("rdp" matches "Redeploy production"). Clicking a result runs it and closes the palette. Show "No commands match" when nothing matches

↑ / ↓ move a highlighted item (wrapping at the ends, hover also highlights), Enter runs it and closes. The input has role="combobox" + aria-activedescendant; items are role="option" with aria-selected
When the palette closes, focus returns to the element that was focused before it opened (e.g. the sidebar link or the search button)

change.title: Group by section
change.html:
"With more commands coming, the flat list is hard to scan."

  • Show results grouped under section headers in this order: Navigation, Deployments, Appearance (SECTIONS in commands.ts). Hide a header when none of its commands match.
  • Arrow keys must follow the visual order across groups.

Hint: build one flat results array in section order and use it for both rendering and the active index.

hints: Global shortcut: document.addEventListener("keydown", ...) in an effect, with cleanup. if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key.toLowerCase() === "k") { e.preventDefault(); ... }
Reuse what exists: <Modal label="Command palette" onClose={onClose}>…</Modal> and commands.filter((c) => { return fuzzyMatch(c.label, query); }).
Render the palette only while open (let palette = null; if (open) { palette = <CommandPalette … />; }): unmounting resets its state, and autoFocus focuses the input on every open.

Arrows (Next): e.preventDefault() (otherwise the cursor jumps), then setActive((i) => (i + 1) % results.length). Reset active to 0 in the input's onChange. Search: "aria-activedescendant combobox mdn".
Focus restore (Next): store e.target from the keydown (or the button from the click) in a ref when opening; useEffect(() => { if (!open && ref.current) { ref.current.focus(); } }, [open]);
Grouping (change): SECTIONS.forEach((s) => { commands.forEach((c) => { if (c.section === s && fuzzyMatch(c.label, query)) results.push(c); }); });
rubric: Open state in App; palette state local and reset by unmounting
Results derived with the existing fuzzyMatch; Modal reused; active index reset on query change
Keyboard handling with preventDefault where needed, wrapping
ARIA: combobox input, listbox / option, aria-activedescendant
Listener cleanup; no stale closure bugs on the toggle
Focus returns to the previous element
Grouping keeps keyboard order equal to visual order

notes: h 38 · radius 8 · active: panel-2 + 2px accent bar

primitives.name: Global keydown listener
primitives.note: Remove the same function you added, in the cleanup. If the handler reads state, list it in the deps so the listener is re-added with fresh values.

primitives.name: Modifier keys + preventDefault
primitives.note: metaKey is ⌘ on Mac, ctrlKey is Ctrl. e.key is uppercase when Shift is held, hence toLowerCase().

primitives.name: autoFocus
primitives.example: <input className="palette-input" autoFocus value={query} onChange={...} />
primitives.note: Focuses the input when it mounts. Combined with "only render while open", the input is focused on every open.

primitives.name: Unmounting resets state
primitives.example:
// closed: <CommandPalette> unmounts, its useState('') is thrown away
// opened again: it starts fresh with query ''
primitives.note: A component's state lives only while it is rendered. Conditional rendering is the simplest "reset on open".

dc45.title: Budget grid: editable cells
dc45.summary: Turn a read-only budget table into a small spreadsheet: click-to-edit cells with Enter / Escape / blur and a live Total column; then Tab navigation, column totals and deleting rows.
dc45.brief:
Ledgerly shows a quarterly budget. App.tsx has AppHeader, BudgetTable and App; getBudget() takes 0.4–1.0 s. The data side is done: App stores each row as GridRow with the cells as text (so "abc" can be kept), and handleCellChange(row, col, text) is already passed to BudgetTable as onCellChange.

Read utils/money.ts: formatMoney, parseAmount (returns null for text that is not a number) and sumAmounts (adds up a list of cell texts, skipping invalid ones). Right now the cells are plain text. Make them editable like a tiny spreadsheet.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Change: delete rows (~24 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan · 7–24 Core · 24–28 change · 28–33 Next · 33–35 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Editing is UI state, so it lives in BudgetTable: editing: { row, col } | null plus a draft string; only one cell is an input at a time, every other cell is a <button> (focusable for free). One commit(next) saves the draft through onCellChange and either starts editing next or stops: Enter commits and moves down, blur commits, Escape just drops the draft. The row Total is sumAmounts(row.cells) in the render: derived, never stored.

Next: Tab / Shift+Tab compute the next position with wrapping (and preventDefault, or the browser moves focus), and the footer column totals map over the months."
requirements: Clicking a cell turns it into a focused input with its current value (only one cell edits at a time). Enter saves and moves to the cell below (or stops editing on the last row). Escape cancels. Clicking elsewhere (blur) saves. Save through the existing onCellChange
A Total column at the end of each row: sumAmounts(row.cells) formatted with formatMoney, derived (never stored), so it updates on every edit
Tab saves and moves right, wrapping to the first month of the next row; Shift+Tab moves left. Focus never leaves the grid while tabbing between cells
A footer row (<tfoot>) with the column totals and a grand total, all derived

Text that is not a number (e.g. "abc") is kept and shown in a red-highlighted cell (title "Not a number"), left out of totals, and a message says "1 cell needs a number. They are left out of the totals." Plus a + Add row form under the table ("New category", disabled when empty; new rows start empty = $0)

change.title: Delete rows
change.html:
"Finance wants to drop advertising this quarter."

  • Each row gets a × button at the end (aria-label="Delete {category}"). All totals update.
  • Stop editing when a row is deleted, and show "No categories. Add one below." if the table becomes empty.

Watch out: if you store the editing position by index, deleting a row shifts indexes. That is why you stop editing.

hints: Editing state in BudgetTable: const [editing, setEditing] = useState<CellPos | null>(null); and const [draft, setDraft] = useState("");
Render: if (isEditing) return <td><input autoFocus ... /></td>; otherwise a <button> inside the td (keyboard-focusable for free).
One commit function: function commit(next: CellPos | null) { onCellChange(editing.row, editing.col, draft); if (next) startEdit(next.row, next.col); else setEditing(null); }
Totals: sumAmounts(row.cells) per row; per column (Next): months.map((m, col) => sumAmounts(rows.map((r) => r.cells[col]))).
Tab (Next): e.preventDefault() first, or the browser moves focus to the next button. Search: "mdn keydown Tab preventDefault".
rubric: Explained why cells are stored as raw strings (invalid input stays visible)
Single editing position; draft separate from committed value
Enter / Escape / blur (and Tab / Shift+Tab) behave as specified
Totals derived with sumAmounts, invalid cells excluded
Reused onCellChange, formatMoney, sumAmounts instead of re-writing them
Row delete clears editing (index shift) and updates totals
Accessible: real buttons and labelled inputs

notes: danger-soft bg · 1px danger ring · danger text
input h 34 w 200 · button h 34 brand

primitives.name: State that can be null
primitives.note: The union says "a position, or nothing". Check !== null before reading .row; TypeScript will remind you.

primitives.name: Enter / Escape / blur on an input
primitives.example:
if (e.key === 'Enter') { e.preventDefault(); commit(nextCell); }
else if (e.key === 'Escape') { setEditing(null); } // draft thrown away
primitives.note: e.key is the key name ("Enter", "Escape", "Tab"). blur fires when focus leaves, including clicks elsewhere.

primitives.name: One column of a 2D grid
primitives.note: Returns a new array with one value per row. Feed it to sumAmounts for a column total (Next).

dc46.title: Theater seat picker
dc46.summary: Select seats on a theater map with a priced summary, then book through the API and recover when a seat gets taken mid-checkout.
dc46.brief:
Lumen Playhouse sells seats for Hamlet. App.tsx has ShowHeader, Legend, SeatGrid, Summary and App. getSeatMap() (0.4–1.0 s) returns every seat with its tier, price and taken flag. formatPrice is in utils/money.ts.

Read bookSeats in api.ts carefully: it takes 0.8–1.4 s and always rejects a booking that includes seat C5 (someone else grabbed it), which also marks C5 as taken on the server. That is how you test the failure path.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Change: max 4 seats (~26 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan · 7–26 Core · 26–30 change · 30–36 Next · 36–38 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"App owns selected: string[] (seat ids, in pick order). The selected seat objects and the total are derived from the map every render. Toggle refuses taken seats; the grid gets selected + onToggle, the summary gets the seat objects and uses the same toggle for ×.

Next: Book calls bookSeats(selected) with a booking flag. Success shows a confirmation and clears the selection; failure shows the error. Either way I refetch the map with a reloadKey state the load effect depends on (one loading path), and after each load I drop selected seats that are now taken."
requirements: Clicking an available seat selects it (gold, aria-pressed="true"); clicking again deselects. Taken seats can't be selected. The legend gets a Selected swatch
The summary lists each selected seat in pick order ("C4 · Standard · $65" with a × remove button) and the Total by tier price, derived from the selected ids (not stored)

The book button reads "Book 2 seats · $160" (disabled with nothing selected) and "Booking…" (disabled) while pending. Success: a banner "Booked! Confirmation LMN-… · seats A5, A6", selection cleared, and the refreshed map shows those seats taken
Failure (any booking with C5): an error banner with the API message, the map is refetched (C5 now taken) and C5 is removed from the selection while the other seats stay selected

Keyboard: only one seat is in the Tab order (roving tabIndex); arrow keys move focus between seats (also across taken seats, stopping at the edges); Enter / Space toggle. Each seat has aria-label="Row C, seat 5, Standard $65" (plus ", taken") and taken seats use aria-disabled so they stay reachable

change.title: Max 4 seats
change.html:
"Box office rule: at most 4 seats per order."

  • A 5th seat is refused with the notice "You can select up to 4 seats." (deselecting a seat clears the notice).
  • The summary header shows the count: "Your seats 2 / 4".

One guard with an early return in the toggle handler, plus one derived label.

hints: Derived: const selectedSeats = selected.map(id => map.seats.find(...)) and total = selectedSeats.reduce(...). Don't store the total.
Toggle: if (selected.includes(seat.id)) { remove } else { add }, with prev.filter(...) / [...prev, seat.id] in the updater. Change: put the 4-seat guard (and an early return) before the add.

Refetch pattern (Next): const [reloadKey, setReloadKey] = useState(0); and the load effect has [reloadKey] deps. Bump it in .finally(); after the map loads, setSelected((prev) => prev.filter((id) => seat is not taken)).
Promise chain: bookSeats(ids).then(...).catch((err: Error) => { setError(err.message); }).finally(() => { setBooking(false); ... });

Roving tabindex (Stretch): focusId state; tabIndex={s.id === focusId ? 0 : -1} (as an if above). Keep refs in useRef<Record<string, HTMLButtonElement | null>>({}) and call .focus() on arrow keys. Search: "roving tabindex".
A <button> already fires onClick on Enter and Space, so you only handle arrows.
rubric: Selection limit enforced with clear feedback
Totals and labels derived from selected ids
Pending state prevents double booking
Failure path: error shown, map refetched, stale selection pruned
Single load path reused for refresh
Roving tabindex + arrow keys + aria labels
Talked about the real-world race (server is the source of truth)

notes: gold bg · dark text · 2px gold glow

primitives.name: Toggle an id in a list
primitives.syntax: if (list.includes(id)) { list.filter((x) => x !== id) } else { [...list, id] }
primitives.note: Both branches return a new array, so they work inside setSelected((prev) => ...). Keeping ids (not seat objects) means the map stays the source of truth.

primitives.name: find() to look up by id
primitives.example:
seats.find((s) => s.id === 'C4')   // { id: 'C4', tier: 'Standard', price: 65, ... }
seats.find((s) => s.id === 'Z9')   // undefined
primitives.note: Returns the first matching item or undefined; check it before use (if (seat) { ... }).

primitives.name: aria-pressed for toggle buttons
primitives.example: <button className={cls} aria-pressed={isSelected} onClick={() => { onToggle(s); }}>{s.number}</button>
primitives.note: Tells screen readers the button is a toggle that is on / off. React renders true/false as the strings "true"/"false".

dc47.title: Comment tree
dc47.summary: Render a forum thread's nested replies at any depth with a recursive component, collapse subtrees, and upvote optimistically with rollback.
dc47.brief:
Threadline is a discussion forum. App.tsx has PostHeader, CommentItem and App. getThread() (0.4–1.0 s) returns comments where each one has replies: Comment[], nested to any depth. Only the top level renders today.

upvoteComment(id, shouldFail) takes 0.4–0.9 s; the existing "Simulate offline" checkbox should be passed as shouldFail. Reuse utils/time.ts (timeAgo) and components/Avatar.tsx.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Change: sort by Top / New (~23 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan · 7–23 Core · 23–30 change · 30–35 Next (or talk).

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"A CommentNode renders one comment and then maps its replies to more CommentNodes: recursion handles any depth. Collapse is local state in each node, because it only affects that subtree. The hidden count is a recursive helper, countDescendants.

Votes I'll lift to App as a map { [id]: true } instead of editing the nested tree: the shown score is score + 1 if voted. Optimistic: set it immediately, call the API, and on failure delete the key and show an error. The map is passed down through the recursion."
requirements: All replies render at any depth with a recursive component; each level is indented with a thread line on the left

Each comment header has a [–] toggle (aria-expanded). Collapsing hides its text, actions and whole subtree, changes the toggle to [+], and shows "4 replies hidden" (all descendants, any depth; "1 reply hidden" for one)
Upvote (▲) increases the score immediately and disables the button (one vote per comment). The API is called in the background
With "Simulate offline" checked, the vote is rolled back when the request fails, the button is enabled again, and a message says the vote could not be saved

change.title: Sort by Top / New
change.html:
"Long threads bury new replies."

  • Add a Sort by select (Top / New) above the comments. Top = highest score first (including your vote); New = most recent first.
  • The sort applies to the top level and to the replies at every level. Collapsed state should survive re-sorting.

Hint: sort a copy ([...list].sort()), never the array from state. Stable keys keep each node's collapsed state.

hints: A component can render itself: inside CommentNode, comment.replies.map((r) => { return <CommentNode key={r.id} comment={r} ... />; }). The recursion stops when replies is empty.
Hidden count: function countDescendants(c) { return c.replies.reduce((sum, r) => sum + 1 + countDescendants(r), 0); }
Votes as a lookup instead of rewriting the tree: const [votes, setVotes] = useState<Record<string, boolean>>({});
Rollback: upvoteComment(id, offline).catch(() => { setVotes((prev) => { const next = { ...prev }; delete next[id]; return next; }); });. Search: "optimistic ui rollback react".
Sorting: [...list].sort((a, b) => displayScore(b) - displayScore(a)) for Top, a.minutesAgo - b.minutesAgo for New.
rubric: Recursive component with stable keys
Collapse kept local and explained why
Descendant count via recursion, derived
Votes lifted to App without mutating the nested tree
Optimistic update uses the updater form and rolls back on failure
Sorting copies arrays; applied at every depth
Mentioned deep trees / performance trade-offs (memo, flattening)

primitives.name: A recursive component
primitives.syntax: function Node({ c }) { ... c.replies.map((r) => <Node key={r.id} c={r} />) ... }
primitives.note: A component may render itself. The recursion stops by itself when replies is empty. Each node gets its own state (collapse).

primitives.name: Recursive function with reduce
primitives.note: Returns a number. Each reply counts as 1 plus everything under it. No reply = the start value 0.

primitives.name: Sort a copy with a comparator
primitives.example:
[3, 10, 1].sort()                        // [1, 10, 3]  (compares as strings!)
[...nums].sort((a, b) => b - a)          // [10, 3, 1]  (highest first)
primitives.note: sort mutates and returns the same array, so copy first. Comparator: negative puts a first, positive puts b first.

primitives.name: Narrow a select value with as
primitives.example:
type SortMode = 'top' | 'new';
<select value={sort} onChange={(e) => { setSort(e.target.value as SortMode); }}>
primitives.note: e.target.value is typed string; as tells TypeScript it is one of your options (only safe because you wrote the <option> values).

dc48.title: Mini form builder
dc48.summary: Build a no-code form editor: add fields and edit label / required with a live preview form; then validation, reordering and a JSON export.
dc48.brief:
Formcraft is a form builder. App.tsx has AddFieldPanel, FieldCard, PreviewPanel and App; getForm() loads two fields after 0.3–0.8 s. The type buttons do nothing yet, the cards are read-only, and the preview is a placeholder.

Read api.ts for the Field type, utils/fieldTypes.ts (FIELD_TYPES, typeInfo, isEmail), utils/id.ts, components/Toggle.tsx (use it for "Required") and components/PreviewField.tsx: it renders one preview field of any type from field, value, error and onChange(value), so you don't have to write the per-type form controls.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Change: JSON export panel (~26 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan · 7–26 Core · 26–29 change · 29–36 Next · 36–38 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The field definitions live in App as Field[]; the builder and the preview both read them. One handleChange(id, patch) merges a Partial<Field>, so label, required (and later options) share it. Add creates a field with a uid and a default label from typeInfo.

The preview is its own component with values keyed by field id, rendering a PreviewField per field. Next: an errors object built on submit by a small validateField, passed to each PreviewField; then move / delete as small immutable helpers."
requirements: The 4 type buttons add a field at the end ("Untitled short text", "Untitled dropdown", …; dropdowns start with "Option 1" and "Option 2"). Each builder card has a label input and a Required toggle (reuse Toggle), both saved through one handleChange(id, patch)

The live preview renders a real form from the fields with components/PreviewField.tsx (it already draws text / email inputs, the select, the checkbox, linked labels and the red *). Preview values are controlled state keyed by field id; builder changes show up immediately

A Submit button validates: empty required fields show "This field is required" (unchecked required checkbox: "Please check this box"), invalid email "Enter a valid email" (pass the message to PreviewField's error). Errors clear as the user fixes the field; a valid submit shows "✓ Submitted…"
Each card has ↑ / ↓ buttons (disabled at the ends) and a ✕ delete button (aria-label="Delete {label}")
Dropdown cards have an "Options (one per line)" textarea that updates the preview's options (PreviewField already ignores blank lines)

change.title: Export as JSON
change.html:
"Engineering wants to paste the form definition into the backend config."

  • Below the preview add a read-only panel "Form definition (JSON)" showing { name, fields } pretty-printed with 2-space indentation.
  • It updates live as the form is edited.

One line of logic: JSON.stringify(value, null, 2) in a <pre>. It is derived, so no state.

hints: One update function: function handleChange(id: string, patch: Partial<Field>) { setFields((prev) => prev.map((f) => f.id === id ? { ...f, ...patch } : f)); } (write the ternary as an if).
Preview values: useState<Record<string, string | boolean>>({}); a checkbox stores a boolean, everything else a string. Update with { ...prev, [id]: value }.
The preview loop: <PreviewField key={f.id} field={f} value={values[f.id]} error={errors[f.id]} onChange={(v) => { setValue(f.id, v); }} />
Validate in submit (Next): loop the fields, build an errors object, setErrors(errors). Use noValidate on the form so the browser doesn't show its own bubbles. Search: "mdn form novalidate".
Options textarea (Stretch): value={field.options.join("\n")} and onChange={(e) => { onChange(field.id, { options: e.target.value.split("\n") }); }}.
rubric: Single source of truth for field definitions shared by builder and preview
Partial-update helper instead of one handler per property
Reused PreviewField, Toggle, FIELD_TYPES and isEmail instead of re-writing them
Preview values keyed by field id (controlled)
Validation computed on submit, errors keyed by id, cleared on edit
Reorder / delete immutable, stable ids as keys
JSON panel derived from state

primitives.name: Partial<T> + spread merge
primitives.example:
const f = { id: 'f1', label: 'Name', required: false };
({ ...f, ...{ required: true } })   // { id: 'f1', label: 'Name', required: true }
primitives.note: Partial<Field> = a Field where every key is optional. Later spreads win, so the patch overrides only the keys it has.

primitives.name: Computed key update
primitives.example:
const id = 'f2';
({ ...{ f1: 'Ada' }, [id]: 'ada@x.co' })   // { f1: 'Ada', f2: 'ada@x.co' }
primitives.note: [id] uses the value of the variable as the key. Pair it with Record<string, string | boolean> for "one value per field id".

primitives.name: JSON.stringify pretty print
primitives.example:
JSON.stringify({ name: 'Beta' }, null, 2)
// '{\n  "name": "Beta"\n}'
primitives.note: Returns a string. The 2 is the indent; null means "no replacer". Show it in a <pre> to keep the line breaks.

dc49.title: Accessible country combobox
dc49.summary: Rewrite a native select as an accessible ARIA combobox for a multi-select field: typing filters, click and keyboard selection, then aria-activedescendant polish and chip keyboard support.
dc49.brief:
Passage is a visa application. Step 2 asks "Countries visited". App.tsx (Steps, App) is done: it loads 40 countries with getCountries() (0.4–1.0 s), keeps visited: Country[], and Save shows "Countries: Japan, France". It renders components/CountryCombobox.tsx inside components/FormField.tsx (read it: the label points at the control via htmlFor, the hint has id {id}-hint).

Today CountryCombobox is a placeholder: a native <select> plus the selected countries as removable chips (toggle, removeChip, chip markup and CSS are there). Rewrite it following the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern, keeping its props. This is a staff-level accessibility exercise: the details are the point.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Change: chips from the keyboard (~32 min).

Timeline: 0–5 read · 5–8 plan · 8–32 Core · 32–36 change · 36–42 Next · 42–45 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Focus never leaves the input. The component owns query, open and the active index; the filtered options and a clamped activeIndex are derived. The input gets role="combobox", aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the listbox id; options get role="option" and ids. Selection stays lifted in App through the existing toggle / onChange.

Keyboard in one onKeyDown: ↓/↑ open or move (clamped), Enter toggles (and preventDefault only then), Escape closes. Options use onMouseDown preventDefault so clicking doesn't blur the input. Next: aria-activedescendant so a screen reader follows the highlight, Home/End, Tab, and scrolling the active option into view in an effect."
requirements: Rewrite CountryCombobox as a text input with role="combobox", aria-expanded, aria-controls (the listbox id) and aria-autocomplete="list", keeping the id prop so the label and hint stay linked. The popup is a role="listbox" with role="option" children (flag + name) and unique ids. Disabled with "Loading countries…" until loaded. Blur closes the list

Typing filters options (case-insensitive "contains") and opens the list with the first option active. Clicking an option or pressing Enter toggles it as a chip (Enter must not submit the form); the text clears and the list stays open. ↓/↑ open the list or move the active option (clamped at the ends); Escape closes. Focus never leaves the input

aria-activedescendant points at the highlighted option while open and is removed when closed; selected options have aria-selected="true" and a ✓; "No countries match" when empty; Home/End jump; Tab closes without selecting; a second Escape clears the text; the active option is scrolled into view
A ✕ clear button (aria-label="Clear all countries") empties the selection and the text and returns focus to the input; clicking anywhere in the box around the chips focuses the input

change.title: Chips from the keyboard
change.html:
"Screen reader users can't tell what they picked, and keyboard users can't remove chips quickly."

  • Backspace in the empty input removes the last chip.
  • Removing a chip with its × button returns focus to the input (the button you clicked disappears).
  • The listbox gets aria-multiselectable="true", and a polite live region announces "3 countries selected".

hints: Read the pattern first. Search: "aria apg combobox list autocomplete" (w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg). Copy its attribute list, not its code.
Keep the active index valid when the list shrinks: const activeIndex = Math.min(active, options.length - 1); and reset to 0 on every keystroke.
Clicking an option blurs the input before the click fires. Fix: onMouseDown={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); }} on each option.
Enter: only preventDefault() when you actually select something; otherwise let Enter submit the form like any input.
Option ids must be unique on the page: id={id + "-opt-" + c.code}. Then (Next) aria-activedescendant={activeId} where activeId is undefined when closed.
Scroll into view (Next): useEffect(() => { listRef.current.children[activeIndex].scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" }); }, [activeIndex, open]); Search: "mdn scrollIntoView block nearest".
rubric: All ARIA attributes correct and wired by id (combobox, listbox, option, activedescendant, expanded)
Focus stays in the input; mousedown preventDefault on options
Complete keyboard map including Home/End, Escape twice, Tab
Active option kept valid and scrolled into view
Value lifted to App; component reusable (props, no global ids)
Chips: remove buttons labelled, Backspace removal, focus returned, live region
Talked about screen reader testing (VoiceOver / NVDA) and the APG

notes: h 38 · radius 8 · active: primary-soft + 3px left bar

primitives.name: aria-activedescendant
primitives.example: • Japan
primitives.note: Points at the id of the highlighted option, so screen readers announce it while real focus stays in the input. Leave it undefined when the list is closed.

primitives.name: mousedown preventDefault keeps focus
primitives.example: <li onMouseDown={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); }} onClick={() => { toggle(c); }}>
primitives.note: A mouse press moves focus (blurring the input, which closes the list) before click fires. Cancelling mousedown keeps focus where it is; the click still happens.

primitives.name: Clamp with Math.min / Math.max
primitives.example:
Math.min(5 + 1, 5)   // 5  (stays on the last option)
Math.max(0 - 1, 0)   // 0  (stays on the first)
primitives.note: Returns the smaller / larger number. Clamping (no wrap) is what the APG combobox does at the ends.

primitives.name: Focus an element through a ref
primitives.note: .current is the DOM node after render (null before). Use it when the focused element is about to disappear, like a removed chip's button.

dc50.title: Virtualized log viewer
dc50.summary: Render 10,000 log lines smoothly by drawing only the visible rows (plus overscan) from scrollTop math, with a sticky header, filters, and jump-to-line.
dc50.brief:
Tracewell is a log explorer. getLogs() returns 10,000 lines after 0.8–1.5 s. Rendering them all freezes the tab, so the starter only shows the first 200. components/LogRow.tsx renders one row and the header, and exports ROW_HEIGHT (26px: every row is exactly that tall). formatNumber is in utils/format.ts.

Build virtualization by hand (no libraries): keep the scroll container's full height, but only render the rows that are on screen.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4–5. Change: jump to line (~31 min).

Timeline: 0–5 read · 5–8 plan · 8–31 Core · 31–38 change · 38–42 Next · 42–45 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The scroller keeps its real height through a spacer div of count × ROW_HEIGHT, so the scrollbar is right. I track scrollTop from onScroll and the viewport height from a ResizeObserver. Then start = floor(scrollTop / H) - overscan, end = ceil((scrollTop + viewport) / H) + overscan, clamped, and I render only slice(start, end), each absolutely positioned at top: index × H.

The header is position: sticky inside the scroller. Filtering is a useMemo over level + text, and virtualization runs on the filtered list, so it stays fast. When the filter changes I reset the scroll to the top."
requirements: All 10,000 lines are scrollable but only the visible rows plus an overscan of ~8 above and below are in the DOM (fewer than ~90 rows at any time). The scrollbar reflects the full list (spacer height = rows × 26px), and the column header stays visible (keep LogHeader inside the scroller; its position: sticky is already in the CSS)

Rows are positioned from scrollTop math (start / end window, top = index × 26), not by rendering everything; scrolling fast never shows blank gaps. Viewport height is measured (and re-measured on resize)
A text filter (message or service) and level buttons (ALL / DEBUG / INFO / WARN / ERROR) filter the list (memoized), and virtualization keeps working on the filtered rows
Changing the filter resets the scroll to the top, and "1,234 / 10,000" shows the match count
Jump errors: "Enter a line between 1 and 10,000" for invalid input, and "Line 42 is hidden by the current filter" when the line is filtered out

change.title: Jump to line
change.html:
"Support pastes a line number from an alert and needs to see it."

  • Add a "Line #" input and a Go button. Go scrolls so that line is in the middle of the viewport and highlights it (accent background + left bar).
  • For now, ignore input that is not a valid, visible line (the error messages are a Next item).

The row may not be rendered yet, so you can't scrollIntoView it. Compute the scroll position from its index instead.

hints: Structure: <div className="log-scroll" ref onScroll> <LogHeader /> <div style={{ position: "relative", height: total }}>{visible rows}</div> </div>
Measure: const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => setViewportHeight(el.clientHeight)); ro.observe(el); and ro.disconnect() in cleanup. Search: "mdn ResizeObserver".
Window: const start = Math.max(0, Math.floor(scrollTop / ROW_HEIGHT) - OVERSCAN); const end = Math.min(rows.length, Math.ceil((scrollTop + viewportHeight) / ROW_HEIGHT) + OVERSCAN);
Each visible row: style={{ top: (start + i) * ROW_HEIGHT }} with position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0 in CSS. Key by line, not by i.
Wrap the filter in useMemo(() => ..., [logs, query, level]): onScroll re-renders often, and re-filtering 10,000 rows each time is wasteful.
Jump: const index = filtered.findIndex((l) => l.line === n); scrollRef.current.scrollTop = index * ROW_HEIGHT - (viewport - header) / 2;
rubric: Correct window math with overscan and clamping
Spacer keeps the true scroll height; rows absolutely positioned
Viewport measured with ResizeObserver, cleaned up
Filtering memoized; virtualization runs on the filtered list
Scroll reset on filter change explained
Jump computes position from index; validation messages
Discussed variable row heights and why libraries (react-window) exist

notes: input w 80 h 30 · Go button accent

primitives.name: Window math: floor, ceil, clamp
primitives.example:
Math.floor(530 / 26)   // 20  (first row on screen)
Math.ceil(1130 / 26)   // 44  (last row on screen, rounded up)
Math.max(0, 20 - 8)    // 12  (never below 0)
primitives.note: floor rounds down, ceil rounds up. Clamp start at 0 and end at rows.length, then rows.slice(start, end).

primitives.name: ResizeObserver
primitives.syntax: const ro = new ResizeObserver(callback); ro.observe(el); ro.disconnect();
primitives.note: Calls you back whenever the element's size changes (and once after observe). clientHeight is the visible height in px. Disconnect in the effect cleanup.

primitives.name: useMemo
primitives.note: Returns the cached result until a dependency changes. Use it for expensive derived data that would otherwise rerun on every scroll render.

primitives.name: Absolute rows in a relative spacer
primitives.syntax: .spacer { position: relative; height: N px }  .row { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: ... }
primitives.note: The spacer gives the scrollbar the full height; each rendered row is placed at its real offset, so only ~40 elements exist.

primitives.name: Set scrollTop yourself
primitives.example:
const top = index * 26 - viewport / 2;
scrollRef.current.scrollTop = Math.max(0, top); // jumps instantly
primitives.note: Assigning scrollTop scrolls the element (this also fires onScroll). Math works even when the target row isn't rendered yet.
